summary: This note describes the 2004 single "Getting Away with Murder" by Papa Roach, the first single from the band's third album of the same name. It marks a shift from the band's earlier nu metal sound to hard rock, with no rapping. The performance-based video was directed by Motion Theory and set in a Stock Exchange Hall, and the song has been used in WWE Tough Enough and several video games, including a clean remix in Gran Turismo 4.
one_line: Papa Roach's hard rock lead single from their third album, known for its video and use in video games and WWE Tough Enough.
key_facts: "Getting Away with Murder" is the first single from Papa Roach's third album, also titled "Getting Away with Murder".
The song marks a new sound for the band, moving to hard rock instead of their previous nu metal sound.
The song features no rapping at all, which was used in Papa Roach's previous singles.
The video is performance-based and shows the band playing in a Stock Exchange Hall.
The video includes sexual imagery that led lead singer Jacoby Shaddix to describe it as "stocks and bondage" in an MTV2 interview.
The video was directed by Motion Theory.
The song is the former theme song for "WWE Tough Enough".
The song was featured in the 2004 video game "" (title left blank in the note).
The song was also featured in the 2005 video game "MX vs. ATV Unleashed".
A clean remix titled "Getting Away With... (Gran Turismo 4 Vrenna/Walsh Remix)" was featured in "Gran Turismo 4".
The Gran Turismo 4 remix was a bit faster than the original.
The Gran Turismo 4 remix toned down the heavily distorted guitars.
The Gran Turismo 4 remix had a backing whisper of the words "getting away" instead of "...with murder".
